To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antiproliferation action of nitric oxides in the hypertrophed myocardium proceeds via a peroxynirite-dependent mechanism.

1) NO-mediated antiproliferation in hypertrophied NN VM is attenuated; 2) NO-mediated antihyperplasia in the infarction model of cardiac hypertrophy is also attenuated; 3) NO-induced peroxynitrate formation is a key mechanism for NO-dependent antiproliferativeness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NO in the antiproliferation of cardiac myocytes.
the effect of nitric oxide on DNA synthesis in neonatal rat ventricle myocytes (NNVMS) and the non-infarction left ventricle in the 1 week post myocardial infarcted (MI) rat.
the role of peroxynitrites in the regulation of cardiac myocyte hypertrophy.
